learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Demonstrate skills for organization, planning, and strategy.
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems.
Express oneself correctly in Spanish, both orally and in writing.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within their field of application.
Develop the ability to work in a team.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge of: algebra and differential equations.

syllabus_topics: Linear Algebra
Introduction: Systems of linear equations. Matrices and determinants
Matrices and determinants. Definitions and properties.
Inverse matrix. Calculation of the inverse matrix using elementary row operations and the adjoint matrix.
Rank of a matrix.
Systems of linear equations.
Gauss and Gauss-Jordan method.
Rouché-Frobenius theorem. Cramer's rule.
Vector spaces
Real vector space. Definition and properties.
Vector subspaces. Intersection and sum of subspaces.
Linear combination. Linear dependence and independence.
Generating system, basis, and dimension.
Coordinates of a vector with respect to a basis. Change of basis.
Euclidean vector spaces: Gram matrix and Gram-Schmidt method.
Linear applications
Linear application. Definition, properties, and classification.
Kernel and image subspaces of a linear application.
Matrices and equations associated with a linear application.
Similar matrices. Similarity theorem.
Diagonalization
Eigenvalues and eigenvectors of an endomorphism and a matrix.
Characteristic polynomial. Eigenspace of an eigenvalue.
Algebraic and geometric multiplicities of an eigenvalue.
Diagonalizable endomorphisms and matrices. Theorems on diagonalization.
Differential Equations
Introduction to the study of differential equations. First-order differential equations
First definitions. Ordinary differential equation. Order of a differential equation. Solution of a differential equation.
First-order differential equations solvable with respect to the derivative: separable variables, homogeneous, linear, Bernoulli.
N-th order differential equations
Linear differential equations of order 'n'.
Homogeneous linear equations.
Linear equations with constant coefficients.
Complete linear equations.
Systems of differential equations
First definitions. Solution of a system of differential equations.
Homogeneous linear systems of differential equations.
Complete linear systems of differential equations.

assessment_methods.method: Written theory test for Linear Algebra
Written problem test for Linear Algebra
Written theory test for Differential Equations
Written problem test for Differential Equations

assessment_rules: To pass the course, the weighted average of all assessment procedures must be 5 out of 10 or higher. It is essential to obtain at least 4 out of 10 in the written theory tests for Linear Algebra and Differential Equations, and in the written problem tests for Linear Algebra and Differential Equations. If any of these minimums are not met, the overall grade will be calculated according to article 19.9 of the UBU Evaluation Regulations. In the second call, failed assessment procedures will be retaken, but the grade for practical activities will be retained from the first call.
